title: Water treatment
description: Ozone is the most effective and eco-friendly water treatment method. 95% of drinking water in Europe is treated with ozone. It does not form dangerous byproducts like chlorine.

drinking-water.title: Drinking water
drinking-water.heroDesc: Drinking water quality standard in developed countries. 95% of water in Europe is treated with ozone.
drinking-water.content:
Drinking water ozonation is the quality standard in developed countries. Ozone destroys all types of pathogens: bacteria, viruses, spores and cysts with up to 99.99% efficiency. Unlike chlorination, it does not form carcinogenic trihalomethanes.

Given the hazards of chlorination byproducts (halogenated compounds), alternative disinfection methods are preferred. Ozone is officially recommended as a safer alternative.

Ozonation improves water organoleptic properties: removes unpleasant taste and odor, improves color. Residual ozone decays to oxygen in 20–30 minutes, leaving no chemical traces.

Recommended residual ozone in drinking water is 0.1–0.3 mg/L. Treatment is effective at any pH found in natural waters.

regulation.label: Drinking water standards:
regulation.text: Given the hazards of chlorination byproducts (halogenated compounds), alternative disinfection methods are preferred. Ozone is officially recommended as a safer alternative.

intro.paragraph1: Drinking water ozonation is the standard method of disinfection in developed countries: the majority of tap water in Europe is treated with ozone. Ozone destroys bacteria, viruses, protozoan cysts and spores with very high efficiency (up to 99.99%) and is significantly more effective than chlorine, especially against chlorine-resistant pathogens such as Cryptosporidium.
intro.paragraph2: Unlike chlorination, ozonation does not form carcinogenic byproducts such as trihalomethanes. It improves the taste and odor of water and reduces color. Residual ozone decays to oxygen within 20–30 minutes, leaving no chemical traces. Recommended residual ozone in drinking water at the consumer tap is 0.1–0.3 mg/L; systems must include proper contact time and, where required, degassing before distribution.
intro.warningText: Residual ozone in drinking water must not exceed 0.1–0.3 mg/L at the point of use. Ozonation equipment must be designed and operated in accordance with drinking water standards, with adequate contact time and degassing so that water supplied to the distribution network meets regulatory limits.

technicalParams.title: Ozonation technical parameters
technicalParams.infoText: Ozone dose of 1-3 mg/L ensures complete water disinfection. At high organic load, the dose is increased to 5 mg/L for oxidation of organic compounds.

steps.title: Pre-treatment
steps.description: Removal of mechanical impurities and suspended solids. Water turbidity should be < 2 NTU for effective ozonation.

steps.title: Ozone generation
steps.description: Production of ozone from purified air or oxygen by corona discharge method. Ozone concentration in gas: 8-12% (from oxygen) or 2-3% (from air).

steps.title: Ozone dissolution
steps.description: Mixing ozone-air mixture with water through ejector or bubbler. Dissolution efficiency: 85-95%.

steps.title: Contact chamber
steps.description: Water retention in contact chamber for 4-10 minutes to complete oxidation and disinfection reactions.

steps.title: Degassing
steps.description: Removal of residual ozone from water before supply to distribution network. Residual concentration: < 0.1 mg/L.

steps.title: Post-chlorination (optional)
steps.description: Addition of minimal chlorine dose (0.3-0.5 mg/L) for prolonged effect in distribution network.

pathogens.title: What ozone destroys in drinking water
items: Bacteria: E.coli, salmonella, cholera vibrio, legionella — 99.99% in 2 minutes
Viruses: hepatitis A, rotaviruses, enteroviruses, noroviruses — 99.99% in 4 minutes
Bacterial spores: anthrax, clostridia — 99% in 10 minutes
Organic pollutants: phenols, pesticides, oil products — oxidation to CO₂ and H₂O
Iron and manganese: oxidation to insoluble forms for subsequent filtration

effectiveness.title: Disinfection effectiveness
effectiveness.highlightBox: Ozone is especially effective against cryptosporidium — parasites causing diarrhea. They are practically resistant to chlorination (requires more than 7200 mg×min/L of chlorine for inactivation), but vulnerable to ozone.

items.title: Safety
